Raidās
(15th century A. D.)
------------------------------------------
Neither God nor his devotees recognise caste (based on birth) as an important factor in social hierarchy. Many great leaders of the भक्ति Movement in the Middle Ages belonged to the lower strata of the society. One such was रैदास् (also called Ravidās and Rohidāsa) who lived in काशी or वाराणसी.
Though born in a family of the cāmār or cobbler caste, रैदास् was deeply devoted to God and tried to lead a pure life. Driven out of the होउसे by an enraged ड़थेर् who could hardly understand his spiritual aspirations, he set up his own home and business along with his equally pious wife.
Hard-working and honest, he spent much of his time in singing the names and glories of God.
He was one of the disciples of Svāmi रामानन्द (14th century A. D.), the then famous saint of काशी, and was a friend of कबीर् (A.

-1518), another disciple of the same teacher.
Mīrābāī (A.

-1614), according to some sources, was a disciple of his, as also the then queen of काशी. The former, however, is unlikely if he were a disciple of Svāmi रामानन्द.
Some of his compositions like ‘prabhujī tum चन्दन ham pānī’ are popular even today.
He is said to have lived for 120 years.
